author: TeIq
content:
## Source
.design/m5/48-tpm-signing.md — REQ-8, AC-6 + decomposition PR 5.

## Surface
- Extend `polaris labeler-key rotate` to detect TPM mode and:
  1. Generate new keypair in TPM under same PCR policy
  2. Publish new `app.bsky.labeler.service` record
  3. Insert old public key into `revoked_keys`
  4. Switch active signer through the existing v1 `active_signer` watch channel
  5. Destroy the old TPM handle (`Esys_FlushContext` + NV erase)

## Rust-quality notes
- Reuses the v1 rotation pipeline (#65) — only the SigningKey-mode-specific work is new. Per rust-quality §9: don't fork the rotation flow.
- **Old-handle destruction is mandatory** — leaving an orphaned handle on the TPM weakens the threat model (a future compromise could potentially resurrect it). Wrap in a transaction-like RAII so partial-rotation failures clean up.
- Per rust-quality §10: rotation runs on `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` (TPM calls are sync); watch-channel publish is async.

## External references
- v1 rotation pipeline: `polaris-backend/src/labeler/rotation.rs`
- v1 active_signer watch channel: `polaris-backend/src/api/state.rs`

## Acceptance (AC-6)
- [ ] End-to-end: rotate in TPM mode → new keypair generated → old destroyed → labels emitted post-rotation verify under the new key.
- [ ] Pre-rotation labels still verify under the old key (which lives in `revoked_keys`).

## Blocks / blocked-by
- Blocked by #158.
- Blocks #160 (reseal-after-update is the recovery counterpart to rotation).
